```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("theme.R")
library(housepi)
set.seed(42)
```

In this vignette we present all available options for the choice of the prior and Monte Carlo proposal in `housepi`. 

# Continuous priors

To perform the sampling we consider the "blank" model, i. e. a data independent template model, with log-likelihood always equal to zero.
Here's the full list of available continuous distributions present in `housepi`:
```{r}
#| warning: false
# create an instance of the blank model
new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  # continuous distributions in housepi
  load_parameter_list(
    uniform = list(prior = "uniform", min = 0, max = 1),
    normal = list(prior = "normal", mean = 0, sd = 1),
    lognormal = list(prior = "lognormal", meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1),
    gamma = list(prior = "gamma", shape = 2, scale = 1),
    weibull = list(prior = "weibull", shape = 2, scale = 1),
    rayleigh = list(prior = "rayleigh", scale = 1),
    beta = list(prior = "beta", shape1 = 2, shape2 = 1),
    exponential = list(prior = "exponential", rate = 1)
  ) |>
  # perform the sampling with the inference command
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_dens()
```

Here we associated definitions of parameters with default proposals and custom arguments.
For certain distributions, default arguments are also available according to base R.

## Provide a custom range

We then test various example MISSING

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)

new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(default = list(prior = "normal"),
                      below = list(prior = "normal", min = -1),
                      above = list(prior = "normal", max = 1),
                      both = list(prior = "normal", min = -1, max = 1) ) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_dens() +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(0, 0.6)) +
  geom_vline(data = data.frame(Parameter = c("below", "above", "both", "both"),
                               xintercept = c(-1, 1, -1, 1)),
             aes(xintercept = xintercept),
             linetype = 2)
```

# Discrete priors

```{r}
#| include: false
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "orange")
```

Here's the full list of available discrete distributions present in `housepi`:

```{r}
# discrete distributions in housepi
new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(
    poisson = list(prior = "poisson", lambda = 2),
    binomial = list(prior = "binomial", size = 4, prob = 0.5),
    negative_binomial = list(prior = "negative_binomial", size = 4, prob = 0.5),
    geometric = list(prior = "geometric", prob = 0.5)
  ) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_hist(binwidth = 1)
```

## How to discretize continuos priors

Previous continuous priors can be chosen to be discretized simply by adding the flag `discr = TRUE`.

```{r}
new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(
    uniform = list(prior = "uniform", discr = TRUE),
    normal = list(prior = "normal", discr = TRUE),
    lognormal = list(prior = "lognormal", discr = TRUE),
    gamma = list(prior = "gamma", shape = 2, discr = TRUE),
    weibull = list(prior = "weibull", shape = 2, discr = TRUE),
    rayleigh = list(prior = "rayleigh", discr = TRUE),
    exponential = list(prior = "exponential", discr = TRUE)
  ) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_hist(binwidth = 1)
```

Note that here we dropped all arguments that allow for a default values. 

# Monte Carlo proposals

```{r}
#| include: false
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "brightblue")
```

```{r}
# available proposals in housepi
proposal_list <- c("sample", "uniform", "normal", "lognormal")
defs <- Map(list, prior = "normal", min = 0, proposal = proposal_list, proposal_scale = 100) |>
  setNames(paste("proposal", proposal_list, sep = "_"))

new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  infer() |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_trace()
```
Note that the proposal "lognormal" does not fit the case of negative values.

## Role of finite adaptation

```{r}
new_housepi_model("blank") |>
  load_parameter_list(from = defs) |>
  infer(adapt = 1000) |>
  get_param_draws() |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_trace()
```
